sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchant Acquiring and Clearing Service Provider (PSP)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong commercial customary law influences; Napoleonic heritage)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
Panama–China BIT (1996, with new negotiation protocols)
Agreement on Exchange of Financial Account Information (CRS Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (as amended by Law 70 of 2019, Law 254 of 2021, and Executive Decree 2021) adopting FATF standards; Resolution No. 129-2023 of the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF) on registration of final beneficiaries; Article 52 of Cabinet Decree No. 2 of 2021 on beneficial ownership of legal persons; the Panama Companies Law (Law 32 of 1927, as substantially amended by Law 4 of 1977, Law 2 of 1982, Law 49 of 2016, and Law 52 of 2016); the Unique Regime of Beneficial Ownership (Régimen Único de Beneficiarios Finales) implemented via the Integrated System for the Unique Tax Registry (SIRUF/SIRE) and regulated by Resolution UAF; AML regime also includes Law 2 of 2011, Decree 1 of 2013, and the Specific Regulation on Client Due Diligence for non-financial sectors.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (integrated into SINCO by the General Directorate of Companies — Registro Público de Panamá; registered agent must file a comprehensive UBO affidavit; public index limited to registered agent confirmation, with full beneficial ownership behind restricted government and tax authority access)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence for each corporate shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (or equivalent foreign corporate registry for non-Panamanian shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or competent authority in the country of origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Statutes (Poderes) of each beneficial owner and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarial authorities in the country of origin or Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating in a Hague state); consular legalization required for non-Hague originating documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport / Government-Issued Photo ID of each ultimate beneficial owner, director, and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity authority of the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on notarial certification of passport copy, or notarized copy certified by Panamanian consul in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address and utility bill of UBO (for KYC/AML file)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or national public registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy witnessed and apostilled; alternatively consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter addressed to Panamanian registered agent (emitida a favor de la sociedad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution of the beneficial owner (QFCB or international bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification plus apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Discharge / Tax Residency Certificate of the ultimate shareholder(s) (for AML profile and CRS determination)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Finance / Tax Administration of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against Panamanian 'PEPs' list published by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) and the National Assembly of Deputies; mandatory OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list screening; mandatory United Nations Security Council Consolidated List screening; mandatory European Union restrictive measures screening; mandatory Panamanian national sanctions list via the Ministry of Finance and UAF; enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, family members, and close associates; risk-based customer due diligence per Law 23 of 2015 Articles 8-12; UBO must be screened before incorporation and on an ongoing basis; electronic verification of identity via third-party risk database required before appointment of registered agent; if any match hits, incorporation must be refused and the transaction must be reported as suspicious transaction (ROS/Reporte de Operación Sospechosa) to the UAF within 24 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sistema de Consulta de Nombre en el Registro Público de Panamá (online name search through Registro Público de Panamá: www.registro-publico.gob.pa); corporate name reservation via registered agent under the 'Aviso de Reserva de Nombre' system within the Registro Público; shared electronic Filing Service (SINCO) where names are screened in real time.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish or any language using the Latin alphabet; where a name is in a foreign language, a Spanish transliteration or Spanish name may be required only if the registered agent determines ambiguity; recognized suffixes are 'Sociedad Anónima', 'S.A.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.' (with 'S.A.' preferred and statutorily recognized); company name cannot be identical or confusingly similar (similitud que induzca a error) to an existing registered name; geographic or descriptive terms are permitted if not contrary to law and not deceptive; ISIC 6619 payment gateway enterprises should avoid names containing 'Banco', 'Financiera', 'Trust', 'Fiduciaria', 'Seguros', 'Reaseguros', 'Crypto', 'Exchange' without licensing or prior authorization to prevent automatic rejection by the registry scanning algorithm.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a proposed name (or the SINCO system flags a prohibited token), the registered agent may file a written reconsideration petition (Escrito de Recurso de Reconsideración) with the Directorship General of Companies within 5 business days of the rejection notice, citing Article 41 of Law 38 of 2000 (Administrative Procedure Law). If the initial rejection is sustained, the applicant may file an appeal (Recurso de Apelación) with the Junta Directiva del Registro Público within 10 business days of the reconsideration decision. Prior ministerial authorization may be required for sensitive tokens; the ministerial approval must be attached to the name reservation. If the name is reserved and not incorporated before the expiration of 30 days, the reservation lapses; a new reservation may be filed on the next business day. Reservation extension of up to 30 additional days may be sought by filing a renewal request with payment of registry tariff (approx. USD 25–50) before the reservation expiration date, but final acceptance remains at the discretion of the Registro Público.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permitted for general corporate registry purposes (registered agent service, mailing address, and virtual office arrangements) under Panama law; a registered agent must have a physical Panamanian address. However, for a cross-border payment gateway company operating under ISIC 6619, the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) and the UAF require a substantive local operational presence or a qualifying foreign jurisdiction model. Pure virtual office (shared workspace without dedicated staff and director meetings) will not satisfy the SBP's licensing expectations if the entity becomes a licensed PSP; for a non-licensed B2B payment gateway entity that merely holds contracts and uses foreign processing partners, a virtual office can satisfy merely the corporate registered agent requirement, but the company should maintain a registered agent address distinct from a shell-mail concept, with a physical presence capable of receiving inspections. Acquiring a banking license or PSP authorization under Title III of Legislative Decree 2 of 2008 (SBP) is generally not feasible with only a virtual office; physical office and local compliance officer (Oficial de Cumplimiento) presence are mandatory for a licensed PSP.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: HIGH_MEDIUM / 70% annual inspection probability for a payment gateway entity due to FATF and UAF high-risk scoring. The SBP conducts on-site visits for licensed financial entities at least every 12 months, and UAF may inspect registered agents and PIFs/SAs that process payments or have high AML exposure; the registered agent must produce physical board minutes and accounting records upon inspection; foreign-management model with zero physical records in Panama is assessed as a significant compliance deficiency.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Panama S.A. standard incorporation fee (registered agent professional fee for drafting articles and statutory filings)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Agent (law firm or licensed corporate services provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in Panama City; not fixed by statute; includes SINCO filing, registry tariff, and registered agent appointment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Público de Panamá incorporation inscription treasury tariff (derecho de inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Registro de Sociedades)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Registro Público fee schedule (Arancel del Registro Público), payable upon presentation of the Escritura Pública de Constitución

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for corporate charter (Escritura Pública de Constitución) before Panamanian Notary (Notario Público)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian Notary (licensed attorney with notarial slot)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff regulated by Law 53 of 2015 and Colegio de Notarios de Panamá fee schedule (approx. USD 75–150 per normative document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation fee (Aviso de Reserva de Nombre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registro Público tariff schedule (derecho de aviso/reserva, approximately USD 18–25)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent annual fee (Cargo de agente residente) for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Agent (licensed Panamanian attorney or CP firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; statutory obligation under Law 32 of 1927 art. 4 and Law 52 of 2016 requiring permanent registered agent in Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO initial registration filing at SINCO (Régimen Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / SIRUF (Unique Beneficial Owner Registry system fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee established by Resolution UAF and Registro Público; includes UBO electronic declaration and validation of threshold data

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening package (OFAC/UN/EU/UAF/domestic PEP lists, source: LexisNexis/World-Check or experienced compliance firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance data vendor / law firm compliance department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per corporate due diligence file; not statutory; includes encrypted file and risk score report

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of shareholder and UBO identification bundle (up to 6 documents; foreign-issued passports, company charters, tax residence certs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notarization authorities, respective Ministries of Foreign Affairs/Consulates; fees vary by issuing state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille certificate statutory fees (e.g., US$10–65 per document, EU countries €20–80, consular legalization $100–200 per document) plus courier and agency fee; estimated bundled average

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English/Spanish translation of apostilled corporate and ID documents (when not in Spanish or not in Latin script)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian sworn translator (traductor jurado / traductor público)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-word or per-document market rate; approved translators' tariff; approximately $25–45 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LPOA (Limited Power of Attorney) validation and notarization for corporate signatories beyond registered agent (apoderado generalísimo)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian notary and registered agent attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and market professional fee; statutory fixed stamps and authenticated signatures

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Público tariffs for directors/officers appointment and certificate issuance after incorporation (Certificado de Registro / Ficha)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff for certificates and annotation of appointments (approximately $40–75 per certificate; total 2 certificates)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration (RUC – Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and DGI business registration via SIR tax platform (does not include substantive tax licences)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee/zero statutory fee for obtaining RUC; platform handling fee included in registered agent professional charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cumulative provisional contingency fund for regulatory submission stamps, courier and additional notarial copies (Escritura first and second protocol book)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency based on fixed statutory protocol fees and shipping costs; reserve of 10% of total incorporation costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades de Panamá (Law 32 of 1927, as amended), Title I, Chapter II concerning constitution of the Sociedad Anónima; complemented by Acuerdo No. 3 de 2015 (Rules of the Registro Público) and the Código Fiscal provisions on the annual franchise tax (Law 181 of 2021).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General, Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Juridical Persons Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social Constitutivo / Escritura de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima: a private instrument ratified before a Notary Public and submitted electronically through the E-Registro portal for inscription in the Juridical Persons Section.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Articles customarily state a nominal issued capital of US$10,000 divided into 10,000 registered shares of US$1.00 par value. Paid-in capital may be zero or contributed in kind, with no escrow, deposit, or capital duty requirement at incorporation. An annual franchise tax applies: US$300 for societies with net assets exceeding US$150,000 and US$150 for smaller societies (Law 181 of 2021).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 1 OF THE ORGANIZATIONAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INSERT COMPANY NAME] S.A. - The undersigned Board of Directors, lawfully convened pursuant to Law 32 of 1927 and the Articles of Incorporation, unanimously resolves as follows: (1) The subscription and allotment of ten thousand (10,000) ordinary shares, par value US$1.00 each, is ratified, and issuing officers are directed to execute share certificates in favor of the subscribers recorded in the Share Register; (2) The registered office is established at the address of the resident agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama, where the minute book, share register, and accounting records shall be maintained; (3) [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary, and Treasurer, respectively, each empowered to represent the Company and execute all corporate acts. Unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and official reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Electronic Registry (E-Registro online portal, www.e-registro.gob.pa).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search for three proposed corporate names through the E-Registro portal using the licensed attorney's registered user account; verify that no identical or confusingly similar name exists in the juridical persons database; pay the search fee; and request the Certificado de Reserva de Nombre (name reservation certificate), valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Digital application signed by the incorporator
Three proposed corporate names (primary and two alternates)
Copy of the passport or identity card of the applicant and of the incorporating attorney
Receipt of the name search and reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, file a reconsideration petition with the Dirección General del Registro Público or promptly select an alternative proposed name; the reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría del Circuito), Panama City.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators (at least two individuals, or one corporate incorporator represented by a natural person) ratify the private instrument of incorporation before the Notary. The instrument contains: legal form (Sociedad Anónima), corporate purpose covering merchant acquiring and cross-border payment gateway services, capital structure of 10,000 shares of US$1.00 par value, appointment of the first directors, designation of the resident agent, and acceptance of the registered office. Signatures are authenticated and the instrument is protocolized.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation / Pacto Social
Passports or identity cards of the incorporating parties
Letters of acceptance of the resident agent and of resident directors
Notarization fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary observes missing data or defective clauses, the incorporators execute a clarifying addendum before the same Notary; no new name reservation is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic inscription of the corporation at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Juridical Persons Section).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the E-Registro portal, the attorney uploads the protocolized Escritura Pública together with the registry cover sheet, the resident agent's acceptance, and the official tariff payment receipt. The Registry performs legal review and assigns a corporate folio number. Standard review takes seven business days; an express procedure reduces the term to three business days.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Resident agent acceptance form
Certificate of name reservation
Official tariff payment receipt (derechos de inscripción)
Power of attorney granted to the incorporating attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inscription is returned with caveats (anotación preventiva or observaciones), the attorney cures the observations within 15 calendar days by filing a written correction and, where applicable, a supplementary deed; otherwise the filing lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Legal Existence Certificate and certified copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Certification Section (Certificación y Copias).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the inscription is recorded, request the Certificado de Registro y Personería Jurídica (certificate of registration and legal existence) together with certified copies of the Articles of Incorporation and the registered directors. These records evidence the company's existence for all bank, tax, and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Application letter on attorney letterhead
Corporate folio number of the inscribed society
Payment receipt for the certification fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, file a correction request with the Registro Público citing the original inscription; corrected issuance is generally immediate once the record is rectified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and municipal registration (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), and Municipio de Panamá - Dirección de Rentas Municipales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application through the SIA-CEDI virtual platform of the DGI, submitting the constitution instrument, by-laws, registered office address, and the legal representative's identity card. Thereafter file with the Municipality to obtain the Aviso de Operación for the class 'Servicios de Tecnología y Pagos Electrónicos' and pay the patente municipal fee; evidence of the commercial lease is required.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Personería Jurídica
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney and identity card of the legal representative
Lease contract or title over the commercial premises
Completed RUC application form and municipal business license application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or Municipality questions the activity classification, submit an amended application specifying ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320; if a formal assessment is issued, file an administrative appeal with the MEF Tax Appeals Directorate within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical installation clearance: fire safety, structural, and occupational health inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Municipio de Panamá - Engineering Section; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the commercial office and data operations room, engage a licensed Panamanian engineer to certify structural load where a fit-out is performed; obtain the Fire Safety Prevention Certificate (Aprobación de Prevención de Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos after inspection of emergency exits, extinguishers, and electrical panels; and complete the MINSA occupational health registration for the premises.
required_dossiers: Floor plan and description of fire suppression and exit arrangements
Cuerpo de Bomberos inspection request
Engineer's structural certificate, if load-bearing elements are modified
Occupational health and safety program per Decreto Ejecutivo No. 96 de 1995
Municipal occupancy permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies deficiencies, correct the findings and request re-inspection within 10 working days; installation of required fire-fighting equipment is evidenced by an auditable install certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational governance meeting and issuance of share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The incorporated company itself - organizational meeting of the Board of Directors recorded in the corporate minute book (Protocolo de Sociedad).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators convene the organizational meeting in Panama City; the Board adopts the by-laws (Estatutos), accepts the resignation of founding incorporators where relevant, appoints the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, approves the First Board Resolution, issues physical share certificates, and opens the Share Register and minute book at the registered office. Banking resolutions are executed to open the operating account with a licensed Panamanian bank.
required_dossiers: Notice and agenda of the organizational meeting
Draft by-laws (Estatutos)
First Board Resolution
Share certificates and share register
Officer acceptance letters
Bank account opening questionnaire and KYC documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director cannot attend, a written waiver and proxy under Law 32 of 1927 is valid; a supplemental board resolution may ratify any act performed by the appointed officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Specialized PSP licensing, AML/CFT registration, and card-network approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) - Non-Bank Financial Institutions and Fintech Licensing Division; Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for AML/CFT registration; Visa and Mastercard Payment Facilitator registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the SBP application for the Payment Service Provider license covering merchant acquiring and cross-border payment gateway activities, including the business plan, AML/CFT manual aligned with Law 23 de 2015, capital and liquidity plan, fit-and-proper declarations, and corporate governance documents. Concurrently enter the sponsoring bank's payment facilitator onboarding for Visa and Mastercard direct rails, register with the UAF as an obligated subject, and ensure segregation of customer funds in a Panamanian trust account.
required_dossiers: SBP license application form
Executed AML/CFT compliance manual
Certified capital and liquidity plan
Criminal background certificates of shareholders and directors
Sponsor acquiring agreement with a Panamanian bank on Visa/Mastercard networks
Corporate governance and fit-and-proper declarations
UAF registration certificate as a payment services company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SBP issues a Notice of Deficiencies, the applicant has 15 business days to cure with supplemental information; a denial may be challenged through reconsideration before the SBP Board and thereafter before the Administrative Litigation Courts under the SBP regulatory regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) - Non-Bank Financial Institutions and Fintech Licensing Division, co-administered with the Municipio de Panamá for the Aviso de Operación.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Empresa de Servicios de Pago (Payment Services Company License) covering merchant acquiring and cross-border payment gateway operations under ISIC 6619, together with the Municipal Aviso de Operación for the physical office and Visa/Mastercard Payment Facilitator registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV (Actividad de Bajo Impacto Ambiental): Ficha de Registro Ambiental required; a Full Environmental Impact Study (EIA) is not triggered for an office-based payment gateway with no industrial discharge, no combustion source, and no hazardous process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: sanitary discharges only, to municipal sewer, meeting Decreto Ejecutivo No. 57 de 1992 limits (BOD5 not exceeding 150 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 150 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0, no toxic pollutants); Emissions: no stationary combustion or VOC thresholds triggered; HVAC refrigerants must comply with Law 116 de 2013 and Montreal Protocol obligations; Waste handling: e-waste (servers, batteries, and electronics) must be disposed of through MiAMBIENTE-registered hazardous waste handlers under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 229 de 1996, with manifests retained for at least 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Aprobación de Prevención de Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural loading certificate from a licensed Panamanian engineer for office fit-out; municipal building occupancy permit; MINSA occupational health registration under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 96 de 1995; and Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) employer registration for all personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; electronic services portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://www.dgi.gob.pa), with taxpayer self-service portal for RUC administration and returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign payment-service provider must form or register a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) through a licensed resident agent, register the company with the Public Registry, and then apply for the unified tax identifier number (RUC - Registro Único de Contribuyentes) at the DGI. The application requires the notarized and registered public deed, corporate bylaws, appointment of the resident agent, certified list of directors and shareholders, local fiscal address, and any banking/AML references required for the high-risk PSP licence. The RUC integrates corporate income tax, ITBMS, withholding tax, and municipal tax obligations. Non-resident ownership is permitted and there is no minimum paid-in capital.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box election and does not provide hybrid mismatch entity classification elections. A Panamanian S.A. is taxed on Panama-source income only; foreign-source income is outside the corporate income tax base. Available administrative elections include voluntary or mandatory registration under the small-taxpayer ITBMS regime for persons with annual gross income at or below B/.36,000 and election of the DGI-authorized e-invoicing model (FEL - Facturación Electrónica en Línea). Certain qualifying companies in Panama's special regimes (e.g., SEM, City of Knowledge) may elect special tax treatment. No domestic hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's VAT-equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (36,000 Panamanian balboas / US dollars) in annual taxable turnover. Taxpayers with annual gross income above this threshold must register for ITBMS; taxpayers below the threshold may register voluntarily or, if otherwise carrying on a taxable activity, may qualify as small taxpayers (pequeño contribuyente).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica en Línea - FEL) applies to ITBMS-registered taxpayers, phased in under Law 49 of 2018, based on taxpayer size and activity. Invoices and credit/debit notes must be issued as structured XML documents through a DGI-authorized technology provider or the DGI's own platform, transmitted electronically to the DGI for immediate validation, and must carry a unique invoice number, QR code, and DGI security code. The payment gateway, as a high-volume automated B2B service provider, must integrate its systems with the DGI through API/Web services for near-real-time submission and receipt of the DGI acceptance response.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ITBMS is available for exports of goods (actual shipment out of Panama) and for exports of services, including financial/payment processing services, where the service is rendered to a non-resident recipient, is effectively used or exploited outside Panama, and is not attributable to a Panama permanent establishment. For a cross-border payment gateway, qualifying services include merchant acquiring, clearing and settlement, transaction switching, and related processing services supplied to foreign financial institutions or foreign merchants, provided the recipient is established abroad and the consideration is paid from non-Panama sources. Written contracts, invoices, bank settlement records, and if required, a DGI export-of-services declaration, must evidence the non-Panama use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA) for physical goods
Bill of lading, airway bill, or other transport document proving physical export
Commercial invoice and export contract evidencing the cross-border transaction
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit statement showing payment received from a foreign account
DGI export-of-services documentary file where services are zero-rated, including service contracts, performance evidence, and confirmation of foreign use/benefit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama's DGI applies strict audit scrutiny to zero-rated export transactions. Absence of the required export documentation or false claims trigger retroactive re-characterization of the zero-rated sale as subject to ITBMS at 7%, plus monthly default surcharges (up to 1.5% per month), correction interest, and administrative fines ranging from B/.500 to B/.50,000 or a percentage of the omitted tax (up to 100%-300%) depending on the offence. Fraudulent issuance of export invoices, forged customs declarations, or use of offshore routing to disguise Panamanian consumption, may additionally constitute tax fraud under the Código Fiscal and Law 49 of 2018, with criminal penalties including monetary fines and incarceration of responsible directors, corporate officers, or resident agents. The DGI's general statute of limitation for tax assessments is up to five years, extended where the taxpayer fails to register or files false returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central issuing monetary authority by constitutional design. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) performs banking supervision and acts as the de facto monetary regulator of the financial system; the Banco Nacional de Panamá operates as the Government's fiscal agent, clearing and settlement bank, and final-credit guarantor for public-sector balances. The national currency, the Balboa (PAB), is fixed at par 1:1 with the US dollar (USD) under Law 84 of 1904; no Panamanian paper or coinage circulates and USD is legal tender throughout the Republic. Consequently, foreign-exchange policy is a passive function of USD liquidity and the domestic banking system rather than an actively managed control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current- and capital-account convertibility. The SBP neither clears nor licences exchange transactions; capital injections, share redemptions, dividend distributions, intercompany loans, royalty payments and profit remittances may all be effected freely in USD without surrender obligation or official approval. Income-tax frictions are minimal under the territorial system: foreign shareholders of a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima generally face no Panamanian withholding on dividends paid from Panama-source profits. However, the Ley 254 de 2022 tax reform widened the income base for entities conducting cross-border payment activities; dividend distributions made from profits attributable to newly taxable non-Panama income may attract a 5% dividend withholding tax, and the treasury should therefore maintain segregated maps of Panama-source versus foreign-source profits to preserve clear remittance economics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio in Panama because there is no central bank monetising foreign exchange. Exporters and service providers, including a payment gateway exporting payment services, may retain 100% of receivables in USD or any convertible currency onshore or offshore, subject only to normal commercial bank AML/CFT large-value declaration filings and, where applicable, tax information filings with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI). Trade-statistics obligations are limited to customs declarations filed through the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas and do not impose any FX repatriation or conversion requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Demand Deposit Account (USD) with SWIFT correspondent access, primary treasury and settlement account
Multi-currency operating account (USD / EUR) plus segregated merchant settlement sub-accounts for domestic clearing
Commercial treasury account for licensed PSPs: payments, receivables concentration and escrow pass-through ledgering
Card-acquiring settlement account (dual collected funds) aligned with Visa / Mastercard brand participation
Capital escrow and legal-fiscal agent custody account for the Sociedad Anónima's paid-in capital subscription

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium, legally constrained. Decreto-Ley 9 de 1998 reserves deposit-taking and funds intermediation to SBP-licensed entities; an offshore electronic-money institution (EMI) has no licensing pathway in Panama and cannot lawfully constitute the gateway's regulated clearing bank. An EMI may only be used as an ancillary acquirer or payout facilitator abroad; client balances and gateway settlement must remain booked at an SBP-licensed institution to preserve fund segregation and bankruptcy remoteness.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is the operative norm. All directors and ultimate beneficial owners must typically attend a physical KYC interview at the bank or at a notary appointed by the bank, produce certified passports and corporate resolutions, and execute specimen signatures before a Panama notary. Remote digital onboarding is generally unavailable for a first-of-relationship PSP account; substitute KYC evidence from a regulated foreign parent or OFAC-compliant correspondent may accelerate a secondary account, but does not remove the SBP's expectation of local in-person validation for high-risk payment operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholders or legacy bearer-share structure obscuring beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registro Público corporate certificate (vigencia) apostilled in the country of issuance; full shareholder ledger showing the chain of ownership; Ley 23 de 2015 beneficial-ownership registry excerpt evidencing the natural persons behind each 25%-plus ownership tier; notarised declaration of source of wealth; written confirmation from the resident agent that all bearer instruments were immobilised or cancelled with the custodian in compliance with the post-2015 bearer-share immobilisation obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentified merchant portfolio, nested-aggregator exposure and high card-not-present velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SBP payment-service-provider licence or formal application receipt; merchant onboarding manual (MBAM) with PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation for every sub-merchant; live sanctions and PEP screening evidence (OFAC, UAF lists); chargeback-ratio and transaction-monitoring architecture; indemnity and anti-money-laundering undertakings signed by each master-merchant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the inbound capital injection funding the gateway treasury
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited IFRS financial statements of the investor; six-month bank statements of the transferring entity; board minutes authorising the equity contribution; notarised declaration classifying the injection as capital and not a loan; legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming that the capital subscription is released from an escrow account only upon satisfaction of the bank's onboarding conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payout rails touching high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geo-blocking and IP-fencing policy for prohibited territories; real-time OFAC and sanctions filtering evidence; payment-route diagram with US, Asian and European clearing nodes; counterparty due-diligence file for each clearing bank and direct merchant; compliance manual certified by the UAF-registered anti-money-laundering compliance officer; commitment letter restricting payout channels to SBP-licensed and OFAC-compliant institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing: (i) subscribe capital by wire to the Sociedad Anónima's escrow account at Banco Nacional de Panamá or a designated Tier-1 bank using SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) with a full 70-character narrative citing the investment purpose, the corporate tax ID (RUC) and the SBP PSP licence application number; (ii) supply the source-of-funds file and beneficial-ownership registry excerpt so the receiving bank may complete its UAF filing without blocking; (iii) instruct funding in USD directly so that no FX conversion leg exists; (iv) release the escrow balance to the operating account only after licence approval and bank acceptance; (v) register the investment with the DGI for territorial-tax classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails available: SWIFT MT103 for standard merchant payouts; MT202 COV for interbank cover payments arising from the gateway's host bank; commercial letters of credit (UCP600 / ISBP745) issued via SWIFT MT700 for trade-instrument relationships with acquiring sponsors; direct Fedwire settlement through a US correspondent bank (e.g., Banco Nacional de Panamá's New York clearing account) for high-value USD finality; domestic low-value clearing through Panama's electronic payment system (SIPE) operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá; and the domestic high-value real-time gross-settlement (RTGS) infrastructure for interbank liquidity transfers. Shortfall liquidity may be sourced through intraday credit lines under the sponsor bank's treasury liquidity policy for gateway settlement flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/CNY, USD/CHF) with SBP-licensed counterparties operating under ISDA 1992 documentation with CSA, permitted for documented gateway revenue streams
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (USD/EUR, USD/CNY) matching merchant settlement receivables with payout commitments, permitted as economic hedges under board-approved ALM policy

Vanilla FX options and zero-premium collars (e.g., EUR/USD and CNY/USD) used to bound conversion risk on non-USD acquiring volumes, permitted where transactions remain alignment-gated to an underlying receivable

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs, e.g., USD/CNY) for exotic merchant-payout currencies through international bank counterparties, subject to the PSP's risk-policy limits and Panamanian general derivative eligibility; NDFs are not required for the USD/Balboa pair because the Balboa is legally pegged 1:1 to USD, creating no FX gap
Pooled liquidity buffers and net-settlement pre-funding accounts held at a US Federal Reserve member correspondent bank, treated as cash equivalents rather than derivatives

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; collected through Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 July for each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late surcharge plus 1% monthly statutory interest on the unpaid US$300 fee; persistent non-payment for five or more consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax / Informational Return (Formulario 101 or equivalent dormant entity declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March following the fiscal year end (for calendar-year entities); within three months of fiscal year end if a different fiscal year is adopted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on any tax due, 1% monthly interest, and administrative fines in the range of US$50 to US$500; continued non-filing may inactivate the taxpayer registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Registro de Beneficiario Final under Ley 70 de 2020)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Central Beneficial Ownership Registry of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, aligned with the franchise tax deadline of 31 July; updated within 30 days after any share transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for failure to file or update the beneficial ownership declaration range from US$200 to US$10,000 depending on severity; the registered agent may also be sanctioned for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PSP Annual Supervisory Report and Audited Financial Statements (SBP-licensed payment service provider)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year end (typically by 31 March for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission exposes the licensee to SBP administrative fines, suspension of the PSP license, and possible revocation of the payment service provider authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audited financial statements are mandatory for SBP-licensed payment service providers, publicly registered companies, and entities required by DGI rules to present audited accounts on the basis of Panama-source revenues or assets; ordinary private S.A. corporations are not automatically subject to a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted by Panama; IFRS for SMEs permitted for entities that meet the applicable DGI size thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Ley 70 de 2020, the registered agent must verify and file an annual sworn declaration confirming the natural-person beneficial owners holding more than 10% interest or exercising control; any share transfer changing beneficial ownership must be recorded in the company's UBO register and reported to the DGI Central Beneficial Ownership Registry within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Bearer Share Certificates (when issued)
Beneficial Ownership Register (Registro de Beneficiario Final)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 700 per annum for the registered agent and registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 5,500 per annum for a licensed PSP entity preparing audited financial statements under SBP requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system exempts foreign-source income from Panama corporate income tax; reduced 15% small-taxpayer rate may apply to legal entities with annual gross revenue not exceeding B/.1.5 million and taxable income not exceeding the thresholds set in the Código Fiscal; no broad fiscal holiday for payment gateway businesses not located in special development zones; expenses attributable solely to Panama-source revenue are deductible under territorial allocation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 740 (Declaración Anual de Renta) filed electronically through the DGI Sede Electrónica at dgi.gob.pa using the taxpayer's RUC and FAN access credentials.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following year, subject to DGI phase-calendar variations by RUC ending digit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source revenue from merchant acquiring, clearing, gateway and processing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only income sourced in Panama; document the foreign-source portion of cross-border payment fees with contracts and flow-of-funds evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source revenue excluded from the taxable base under the territorial income tax doctrine.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting schedules and allocate revenue to the country of the merchant, cardholder or payment rail; foreign-source revenue is not taxed but must be transparently identified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to Panama-source income, including processing system costs, licensing fees, employee salaries and local operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses with valid invoices and banking evidence; transfer pricing adjustments apply to cross-border payments to related service providers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income computed as Panama-source gross revenue less allocable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-controlled Panama S.A., prepare local file documentation if intercompany transactions exceed the transfer pricing threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 25% subject to the applicable small-taxpayer regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax exclusively on Panama-source income; verify whether the 15% small-taxpayer rate is available; otherwise apply 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly estimate payments and withholding tax credits applicable against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-reference Formulario 741 filed during the year; any excess foreign tax credit is not available under territorial taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax balance due or refund resulting from the annual reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any balance due by the statutory deadline; refund claims require full financial statement and source-of-income documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signed by the legal representative and certified by a public accountant for audited taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident director or legal representative in Panama must execute the return; failure to do so invalidates the filing and triggers penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment is subject to DGI surcharge of 5% per month or fraction of delay on the unpaid tax, capped at 25%, plus default interest; additional administrative fines for non-filing may reach B/.5,000; persistent non-observance can trigger RUC suspension, asset attachment and banking restrictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 741 (Declaración de Pago Trimestral del Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed through the DGI Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the 15th day of the month following each calendar quarter; the fourth-quarter liability is included in the annual Formulario 740 reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source revenue for the relevant quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same territorial allocation rules applied in the annual return; keep merchant location and settlement records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable income after deductions for the quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base estimates on the prior-year annual tax return unless a documented change in business activity materially affects revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly income tax payment at 25% (or the small-taxpayer rate as applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure wire transfer references contain the RUC and fiscal period to avoid misallocation of credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative prior quarterly payments for the same fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile payments from DGI receipts; underpayments generate surcharges and interest in the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total amount payable for the quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay from the Panama S.A. bank account; payments made from offshore accounts may raise source and substance risks.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment or late payment of quarterly estimates triggers the same monthly surcharge and interest system applied to the annual return; failure to lodge the quarterly declaration permits DGI estimated assessment on the basis of prior-year income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (withholding tax on dividends paid from Panama-source profits; 0% on distributions of foreign-source earnings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholders seeking a reduced rate under a Panama double taxation agreement must deliver an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the taxation authority of their jurisdiction, provide a beneficial ownership declaration to the Panamanian withholding agent prior to payment, and retain the documentation for at least five years; the withholding agent applies the treaty rate only after the DGI confirms the validity of the residence certificate; if the substance or ownership structure fails, the full 10% domestic rate must be withheld and the relief application becomes subject to audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for Panama-source intellectual property paid to non-residents are generally subject to 10% statutory withholding tax; debt interest paid by a Panamanian entity to a non-resident lender is generally subject to 10% withholding tax when the funds are used in Panama, while interest sourced from foreign borrowing or offshore operations may be exempt under territorial rules; applicable DTA treaty rates commonly range from 5% to 10% for royalties and interest subject to beneficial ownership and TRC conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.3,000,000 (Panamanian balboa, at parity with US dollar) aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; taxpayers with annual gross revenue exceeding B/.10,000,000 are also required to maintain contemporaneous documentation and may be called to present it within 45 days of DGI request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama maintains Economic Substance Regulations under Law 254 of 2021 and related Cabinet Decrees. A Sociedad Anónima operating as a cross-border payment gateway performing operational direction, clearing, settlement and contracting activity in Panama must demonstrate local physical presence, resident management, adequate employees and expenditure proportional to the revenue booked in Panama. Entities with no real substance and only formal registration are treated as shell companies, denied tax residency benefits and exposed to regulatory cancellation. The annual economic substance declaration must be filed with the DGI; failure to comply renders the corporate shell presumption applicable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting Panama-source merchant settlements, omitting gross receipts from local acquiring activities, fabricating deductions or classifying Panama-source revenue as foreign-source without transferable legal basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment of the evaded tax plus monthly surcharge and default interest; administrative fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax; criminal prosecution under the Código Penal carrying imprisonment of two to six years; cancellation of business licenses and RUC suspension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct the revenue misclassification are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and may face criminal imprisonment, judicial travel bans, asset freezes and disqualification from acting as officers of any Panama company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Panama S.A. with no local office, no resident employees, no board meeting records, no operational bank account and no economic substance declaration while treating substantial cross-border payment income as not subject to Panama tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Economic Substance Regulations of up to B/.1,000,000; denial of tax residency status; retroactive disallowance of territorial benefits; judicial liquidation of the company and cancellation of the corporate registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the S.A. is used for tax evasion; directors and nominees become personally liable for the tax and penalties, are subject to civil restitution of distributed assets and may be forbidden from leaving Panama pending criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Cross-Border Payment Activity and Money Laundering (AML/CFT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acting as an online merchant acquirer, clearing house or PSP in and from Panama without the required payment processor license from the Superintendencia de Bancos or the relevant AML authority, and failing to implement KYC, transaction monitoring, and suspicious transaction reporting while processing high-risk or sanctioned payment flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cease-and-desist and regulatory closure; financial penalty up to B/.5,000,000 or 5% of annual transaction volume; criminal asset forfeiture; imprisonment of up to fifteen years under Panama's money laundering statutes; loss of visa and immigration benefits for foreign principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal criminal liability for consenting to or benefiting from unregulated payment flows, preventive detention, travel bans, seizure of personal property, freezing of accounts and long-term disqualification from regulated financial activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Pricing Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File and Master File after surpassing the B/.3,000,000 related-party threshold or engaging in non-arm's-length fees for gateway, licensing, support or commission services paid to the parent or offshore affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may make a transfer pricing adjustment and tax the recharacterized Panama-source income at 25%; administrative penalty of up to 10% of the undocumented related-party transaction amount; assessment of the unpaid tax, surcharges and interest; criminal liability for willful omission in the annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign intercompany arrangements lacking arm's-length substance are personally liable for the resultant tax and penalties; courts may issue civil restitution orders and travel bans against directors who repatriate funds out of Panama without proper economic consideration or documentation.
